US.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
US.what: Free, confidential support for anyone who is thinking about suicide, in emotional distress, or in any crisis, 24 hours a day, every day of the year.
US.label: 988lifeline.org (chat)

US.name: StrongHearts Native Helpline
US.what: A helpline for Native Americans and Alaska Natives hurt by domestic or sexual violence. Advocates answer 24 hours a day, and the helpline describes itself as safe, confidential and anonymous.
US.label: strongheartshelpline.org (chat)

US.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
US.what: Human trafficking means being made to work or to sell sex through force, lies or threats. This hotline connects people who are in that situation, or who got out of it, with support and services to get help and stay safe. It is confidential and open 24 hours a day. The hotline says it is not law enforcement and not an immigration agency.
US.label: humantraffickinghotline.org

US.name: Missing and Murdered Unit (Bureau of Indian Affairs)
US.what: The Bureau of Indian Affairs unit that works on missing, murdered and human trafficking cases involving American Indians and Alaska Natives, together with tribal, federal, state and local police. It also coordinates victim services with families.
US.label: About the Missing and Murdered Unit

US.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
US.what: Live advocates answer by phone, text and online chat 24 hours a day, every day of the year.
US.label: thehotline.org

US.name: National Sexual Assault Hotline
US.what: The national phone line for people who have been sexually assaulted, as listed by the federal Administration for Children and Families.
US.label: Federal list of help lines

US.name: Crisis Text Line
US.what: Free, confidential crisis support by text message, 24 hours a day, from anywhere in the United States.
US.label: crisistextline.org

US.name: National Runaway Safeline
US.what: Free, confidential support for teens and young people who have left home or are thinking about it, 24 hours a day. USA.gov says it can arrange free transportation home or to other safe, stable housing.
US.label: USA.gov emergency housing page

US.name: Indian Health Service, tribal and urban Indian clinics
US.what: The Indian Health Service (IHS), tribal health programs and urban Indian programs give health care to American Indians and Alaska Natives. The IHS says it is not health insurance, and not an entitlement like Medicare or Medicaid.
US.label: IHS Find Health Care

US.name: Urban Indian health programs
US.what: Nonprofit health programs in cities, governed by boards that are at least 51 percent American Indian or Alaska Native. The IHS funds 41 of them, with more than 80 sites in 22 states. Services can include primary care, traditional healing, mental health and substance use counseling, and youth, elder and job programs.
US.label: Map of Urban Indian Organizations

US.name: Purchased/Referred Care: when the IHS pays for care somewhere else
US.what: Care at an IHS or tribal clinic is called direct care. Purchased/Referred Care (PRC) covers medical or dental care away from those clinics. The IHS says PRC is not an entitlement, and a referral does not mean the bill will be paid.
US.label: IHS Purchased/Referred Care

US.name: Health insurance rules for Native people (Marketplace, Medicaid, CHIP)
US.what: Members of federally recognized tribes and Alaska Native (ANCSA) shareholders can sign up for a Marketplace health plan in any month and change plans up to once a month. With income between 100% and 300% of the federal poverty level they can get a plan with zero cost sharing, and they pay nothing for care from Indian health providers at any income. In Medicaid and CHIP, people eligible for IHS services pay no premiums and no out-of-pocket costs for care from IHS, tribal or urban Indian programs. You can keep using those clinics after you enroll.
US.label: HealthCare.gov: American Indians and Alaska Natives

US.name: SAMHSA National Helpline
US.what: Free, confidential information and referrals to treatment for mental health or substance use, in English and Spanish, 24 hours a day.
US.label: SAMHSA National Helpline

US.name: Wellbriety circles (White Bison)
US.what: White Bison is a Native American-operated nonprofit behind the Wellbriety Movement: sobriety, recovery and wellness grounded in Native culture. It keeps a list of Wellbriety circles, which are recovery and talking circles that meet in person and on Zoom.
US.label: List of Wellbriety circles

US.name: Youth Regional Treatment Centers (IHS)
US.what: Residential treatment centers for Native youth who need help with alcohol or drug use, including youth who also have a mental health condition. The Indian Health Service runs some and tribes run others, in Alaska, Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, North Carolina, South Dakota, Washington and other states.
US.label: IHS list of youth treatment centers

US.name: National Indian Child Welfare Association (NICWA)
US.what: Guides and support for Native families dealing with a child welfare case: the Indian Child Welfare Act, kinship care, tracing Native ancestry and finding low-cost legal help. NICWA says it cannot give legal advice or manage individual cases.
US.label: NICWA resource library

US.name: The Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA): your family's rights
US.what: ICWA is a federal law for state court cases about foster care, adoption or ending parental rights when the child is a tribal member, or is eligible for membership and has a parent who is a member. The state must make active efforts to keep the family together, tell the child's tribe and parents about the case, and follow placement preferences that favor family and community. The tribe can join the case, and a parent or the tribe can ask to move it to tribal court. ICWA does not cover custody disputes between parents.
US.label: What is ICWA? (NICWA)

US.name: UNITY: United National Indian Tribal Youth
US.what: A national network of Native youth councils that builds leadership through trainings and conferences. Councils can be tribal, village, urban, school or college groups.
US.label: How to join UNITY

US.name: We R Native: Ask Your Relatives
US.what: A site for Native youth where you can send a question to Auntie or Uncle and read answers to questions other young people have asked.
US.label: Ask Your Relatives

US.name: American Indian College Fund scholarships
US.what: Scholarships for Native students in certificate, undergraduate or graduate programs at tribal colleges and at accredited nonprofit colleges. One application a year covers all of its scholarships.
US.label: College Fund scholarships

US.name: Cobell Scholarship
US.what: Scholarships for undergraduate, graduate and vocational or trade students, to help with tuition, fees, books and living costs.
US.label: cobellscholar.org

US.name: Tribal colleges and universities
US.what: The American Indian College Fund lists 34 accredited tribal colleges and universities, with a page for each. The Bureau of Indian Education runs two of them itself: Haskell Indian Nations University in Lawrence, Kansas, and Southwestern Indian Polytechnic Institute in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
US.label: List of tribal colleges

US.name: No place to stay tonight: emergency shelter
US.what: The federal housing department's direction for anyone who is homeless: dial 211 and press 6 for homeless services. Its Find Shelter tool lists local shelters, food pantries, health clinics and places to get clothing. USA.gov says 211 works in most areas of the United States and gives referrals for emergency housing.
US.label: HUD Find Shelter tool

US.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
US.what: Free and confidential support, 24 hours a day, for veterans who are facing or experiencing homelessness.
US.label: USA.gov: emergency housing

US.name: Tribal housing programs
US.what: Federal housing money for Native communities goes to tribes through the Indian Housing Block Grant. Each tribe names a housing office, called a tribally designated housing entity, to run its programs, which can include housing services for families.
US.label: National Tribal Housing Directory

US.name: Section 184 Indian Home Loan Guarantee
US.what: A home loan backed by HUD for Native borrowers, with a 2.25% down payment. It can be used to buy, build, repair or refinance a home.
US.label: Section 184 for borrowers

US.name: BIA Housing Improvement Program
US.what: Grants to repair, renovate or replace a home for Native families who cannot get housing help from any other source.
US.label: How to apply (BIA)

US.name: Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations (FDPIR)
US.what: USDA foods for households with low income living on reservations, and for American Indian households in approved areas near reservations and in Oklahoma. Many households use it instead of SNAP.
US.label: FDPIR fact sheet (USDA)

US.name: BIA financial assistance and social services
US.what: Help from the Bureau of Indian Affairs when other programs are not available: General Assistance for food, clothing, shelter and utilities; Emergency Assistance after a fire, flood or other disaster (up to $1,500 a household); Burial Assistance (up to $3,500); and payments toward the care of children and of adults who need daily help.
US.label: BIA financial assistance

US.name: 211: local help with food, housing and bills
US.what: 211 connects you to local help with bills, food, housing, utilities, health costs, mental health and substance use. United Way's 211 site says every call is confidential.
US.label: 211.org

US.name: SNAP food benefits
US.what: SNAP helps people with low income buy food. You apply through your state or local SNAP office.
US.label: How to apply for SNAP

US.name: Lifeline: a discount on phone or internet service
US.what: A federal discount of up to $9.25 a month on phone or internet service, or up to $34.25 a month on qualifying Tribal lands. You can qualify if someone in your household gets SSI, Medicaid, SNAP, federal public housing assistance or a Veterans Pension, or if household income is at or below 135% of the federal poverty guidelines.
US.label: LifelineSupport.org

US.name: Native job and training programs (WIOA Section 166)
US.what: The U.S. Department of Labor funds tribes and Native organizations across the country to give job search help, money for education and training, and support services to Native adults and youth.
US.label: Division of Indian and Native American Programs

US.name: Tribal vocational rehabilitation projects
US.what: Tribal governments run vocational rehabilitation projects that help American Indians with disabilities prepare for and get jobs in a culturally relevant way. Services follow an individual plan for employment and may include native healing services. The federal Rehabilitation Services Administration lists 93 projects in 26 states.
US.label: American Indian Vocational Rehabilitation Services

US.name: Finding legal help (Native American Rights Fund guide)
US.what: A guide from the National Indian Law Library to lawyers, legal aid programs and law school clinics that work on Indian law. The Native American Rights Fund is a nonprofit law firm that has represented tribal nations, organizations and individuals since 1970. It cannot take every request, and its lawyers do not handle criminal or family law cases.
US.label: Finding legal help guide

US.name: Free civil legal aid near you
US.what: The Legal Services Corporation funds nonprofit legal aid programs with offices in every state. They help people with low income with civil legal problems such as evictions, safety, income and family matters. Its programs serve households at or below 125% of the federal poverty guidelines.
US.label: Legal Services Corporation

US.name: Contact any federally recognized Nation (BIA Tribal Leaders Directory)
US.what: The Bureau of Indian Affairs lists contact details for each federally recognized Nation, with a map. As of January 30, 2026 it counts 575 federally recognized tribes.
US.label: BIA Tribal Leaders Directory

US.name: Tracing Native ancestry and enrolling in a tribe (BIA guide)
US.what: The federal guide to working out which Nation your family comes from and applying to it. The BIA does not keep a list of enrolled members and does not do family research for people. Each tribe keeps its own records and sets its own rules.
US.label: BIA guide to tracing ancestry

US.name: Indian boarding school records (National Indian Boarding School Digital Archive)
US.what: An archive of digitized boarding school records and student name lists, built by the National Native American Boarding School Healing Coalition so that survivors and descendants can find their families' records. The coalition has also mapped 523 Indian boarding schools.
US.label: National Indian Boarding School Digital Archive

US.name: Elder programs run by tribes (Older Americans Act, Title VI)
US.what: Tribal programs for elders: meals at a meal site or delivered at home, rides, help around the house, information and referral, and support for family caregivers, including grandparents raising grandchildren.
US.label: Services for Native Americans (Title VI)

US.name: Eldercare Locator
US.what: A free national call center from the U.S. Administration for Community Living. It connects older adults and their caregivers to the local Area Agency on Aging and other local help.
US.label: Area Agencies on Aging

US.name: Veterans Crisis Line
US.what: Free, confidential crisis support for veterans and the people who care about them, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
US.label: veteranscrisisline.net

US.name: No VA copays for Native veterans
US.what: Eligible American Indian and Alaska Native veterans do not pay VA copays for health care or urgent care. Copays still apply to domiciliary care, institutional respite care, institutional geriatric evaluation and nursing home care.
US.label: VA: copay exemption

US.name: Native American Direct Loan (VA home loan on trust land)
US.what: A VA loan to buy, build or improve a home on federal trust land, or to refinance one of these loans.
US.label: VA: Native American Direct Loan

CAN.name: Hope for Wellness Help Line
CAN.what: Counselling and crisis help by phone or online chat, 24 hours a day, for Indigenous people anywhere in Canada.
CAN.label: hopeforwellness.ca (chat)

CAN.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
CAN.what: Call or text 988 any time if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone. Free, in every province and territory.
CAN.label: 988.ca

CAN.name: National Indian Residential School Crisis Line
CAN.what: Crisis support, 24 hours a day, for former residential school students and their families, with referrals to other health supports.
CAN.label: Resolution Health Support Program

CAN.name: Jordan's Principle
CAN.what: Funding so First Nations children can get the health, social and education products, services and supports they need, on or off reserve. Named for Jordan River Anderson of Norway House Cree Nation.
CAN.label: Jordan's Principle

CAN.name: Inuit Child First Initiative
CAN.what: Funding so Inuit children have equal access to health, social and education products, services and supports. Free to apply.
CAN.label: Supporting Inuit children

CAN.name: Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB)
CAN.what: Federal coverage for health costs that provincial plans and private insurance do not cover, such as prescription drugs, dental and vision care, medical supplies, mental health counselling and medical travel.
CAN.label: Who is eligible

CAN.name: Friendship Centres
CAN.what: Community hubs for Indigenous people living in cities and towns, with programs in health, shelter, youth, justice and more. Over 100 centres belong to the National Association of Friendship Centres.
CAN.label: Find a Friendship Centre

MEX.name: Línea de la Vida
MEX.what: Línea nacional, gratuita y confidencial, las 24 horas: apoyo en crisis, riesgo suicida, consumo de sustancias y violencia. (Free, confidential national line, 24 hours, for crisis, suicide risk, substance use and violence.)
MEX.label: gob.mx/conasama

MEX.name: Instituto Nacional de los Pueblos Indígenas (INPI)
MEX.what: La autoridad del gobierno federal en asuntos de los pueblos indígenas y afromexicano, con oficinas de representación en los estados y Centros Coordinadores en las regiones indígenas. (The federal authority for Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples, with state offices and regional coordinating centres.)
MEX.label: gob.mx/inpi

AUS.name: 13YARN
AUS.what: A free, confidential crisis line, 24 hours a day, answered by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Crisis Supporters. Run by and for mob.
AUS.label: 13yarn.org.au

AUS.name: Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations (ACCHOs)
AUS.what: Primary health care started and run by the local Aboriginal community through an elected board. NACCHO is the national body for about 150 of them.
AUS.label: Map of health services

AUS.name: Link-Up family tracing and reunion
AUS.what: Help for members of the Stolen Generations to research family records, trace family, and be reunited with family, Country, community or gravesites, with support before, during and after.
AUS.label: Link-Up services (AIATSIS)

AUS.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Services
AUS.what: Community-controlled legal services in each state and territory: advice, court representation and support for people in contact with the justice system. NATSILS is their national body.
AUS.label: natsils.org.au

NZL.name: 1737, Need to talk?
NZL.what: New Zealand's national mental health and addictions line. Free call or text 1737 any time to reach a trained counsellor, or choose to talk with a peer support worker.
NZL.label: 1737.org.nz

NZL.name: Te Kāhui Māngai: directory of iwi and Māori organisations
NZL.what: The government directory of iwi, hapū and marae, with the organizations that represent them and how to reach them.
NZL.label: tkm.govt.nz

NZL.name: Whānau Ora
NZL.what: Navigators (kaiārahi) with local and cultural knowledge help whānau plan, get through a crisis, and connect with the support they need to reach their goals.
NZL.label: Whānau Ora for whānau

BRA.name: CVV: Centro de Valorização da Vida
BRA.what: Apoio emocional e prevenção do suicídio, gratuito e sigiloso, 24 horas, por telefone, chat ou e-mail. (Free, confidential emotional support and suicide prevention, 24 hours.)
BRA.label: cvv.org.br (chat)

PER.name: Línea 113 Salud, opción 5 (salud mental)
PER.what: Orientación y apoyo psicológico gratuito del Ministerio de Salud, las 24 horas, todos los días. (Free psychological support from the Ministry of Health, 24 hours.)
PER.label: gob.pe: Línea 113

CHL.name: Línea de prevención del suicidio *4141
CHL.what: Línea gratuita y confidencial del Ministerio de Salud, atendida por psicólogos, las 24 horas, todos los días. (Free, confidential suicide prevention line answered by psychologists, 24 hours.)
CHL.label: minsal.cl

TWN.name: 1925 Care Hotline (安心專線)
TWN.what: The Ministry of Health and Welfare's suicide prevention line, open 24 hours a day and free to call.
TWN.label: Find A Helpline: Taiwan

PHL.name: NCMH Crisis Hotline
PHL.what: The 24-hour mental health crisis line of the National Center for Mental Health, part of the Department of Health, for anyone in emotional distress or thinking about suicide.
PHL.label: doh.gov.ph

ZAF.name: SADAG Suicide Crisis Helpline
ZAF.what: South Africa's suicide crisis line, run by the South African Depression and Anxiety Group: free, 24 hours a day, with referrals to local help.
ZAF.label: sadag.org

COL.name: Línea 106: teleorientación en salud mental
COL.what: Línea nacional del Ministerio de Salud, gratuita y confidencial, las 24 horas, para apoyo emocional, crisis o simplemente hablar con un profesional de salud mental. (Free, confidential national mental health line, 24 hours.)
COL.label: minsalud.gov.co: Línea 106

ECU.name: Línea 171, opción 6: salud mental
ECU.what: Línea gratuita del Ministerio de Salud Pública para primeros auxilios psicológicos, intervención en crisis y citas de psicología. (Free Ministry of Health line for psychological first aid, crisis help and appointments.)
ECU.label: salud.gob.ec

IND.name: Tele-MANAS (14416)
IND.what: The Government of India's free national mental health helpline, open 24 hours, for counselling, emotional support and referrals, in about 20 languages.
IND.label: Ministry of Health: Tele-MANAS

MYS.name: Talian HEAL 15555 (mental health crisis line)
MYS.what: The national mental health crisis line, run by counselling officers of the Ministry of Health (KKM). It gives emotional support and early help in a crisis, including thoughts of suicide, depression, anxiety, panic and stress.
MYS.label: Find A Helpline: Talian HEAL 15555

IDN.name: AMAN, Aliansi Masyarakat Adat Nusantara
IDN.what: The national alliance of Indigenous peoples in Indonesia. It works for the rights of Masyarakat Adat through its programmes, policy work and campaigns, and has affiliated bodies for youth (BPAN) and women (Perempuan AMAN).
IDN.label: aman.or.id

ARG.name: Línea de salud mental 0800-999-0091
ARG.what: La línea nacional de urgencias en salud mental del Ministerio de Salud: atención gratuita las 24 horas. (Argentina's national mental health urgency line: free, 24 hours.)
ARG.label: argentina.gob.ar

PRY.name: Línea 155 Salud Mental
PRY.what: La línea de crisis en salud mental del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social: gratuita, confidencial, las 24 horas, todo el año, en todo el país. (The Ministry of Health's free, confidential mental health crisis line, 24 hours, nationwide.)
PRY.label: Agencia IP (gobierno): Línea 155

PAN.name: Línea 147, Ministerio de Desarrollo Social (Mides)
PAN.what: Línea gratuita y confidencial de apoyo emocional y orientación en salud mental, las 24 horas, todos los días, para crisis emocionales, ideación suicida y ansiedad. (Free, confidential mental health support line, 24 hours.)
PAN.label: TVN: Línea 147

WORLD.name: Keepers of the Earth Fund (Cultural Survival)
WORLD.what: Grants of up to 12,000 US dollars that go straight to Indigenous communities, collectives, organizations and traditional governments for projects they design themselves. Groups without government registration can apply.
WORLD.label: Keepers of the Earth Fund

WORLD.name: UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues
WORLD.what: The United Nations advisory body on Indigenous peoples' issues: development, culture, environment, education, health and human rights. It meets each year in New York, where Indigenous peoples' organizations can take part.
WORLD.label: UNPFII

WORLD.name: The Indigenous World 2026 (IWGIA)
WORLD.what: A yearly report, free to read, on the situation and rights of Indigenous peoples in more than 60 countries, written mostly by Indigenous and expert authors. The 2026 edition is the 40th.
WORLD.label: Read the report
